facts.fact: Twenty-two's intake name is Kamalakshi; her page is read in the shed with Pavi present.
facts.why: needed because prior chapters promised her a private reading and gave only that it had four syllables.

facts.fact: Thilak's ledger number is Four and his shape is boar. Kuttu is Kumaran, a ferryman's son. Thulasi is a salt-boiler's daughter of Pazhayangadi.
facts.why: needed because the pages are read aloud on the page.

facts.fact: Vellan's intake roll reads 'a joiner's son, of Venmanal, sold at nine'.
facts.why: needed because his page is read aloud; fits his habit of carving.

facts.fact: Kirri's ledger number is Twelve and her intake roll reads 'Kirthika, a boatwright's daughter, of the coast, sold at five'.
facts.why: needed because Neela reads her page at kennel nine.

facts.fact: Muthu brings thirty garrison volunteers against Rema's posted order, burns his unsent grey-wax month letter in the gate fire-basket, and keeps his men facing the road so none witnesses a turning.
facts.why: needed to carry out the outline beat.

facts.fact: Chathu is taken to Kettamala on horseback by Muthu's men, with a gag cloth for after dusk until dawn, so he cannot say any shape aloud.
facts.why: needed because he is first witness to the forty and a living cage-threat.

facts.fact: The forty ride east to the old cairn camp, held by Bhaskaran's men, to wait until the court has spoken. Each took a season's flask. Pachan keeps kennels and groves with no one rationing resin.
facts.why: needed to place the forty offstage for ch 29 and resolve the resin leash.

facts.fact: The cut-away back half of the ledger has many stubs of leaves cut by a clean blade, each marked in the margin with a tiny sunbird with folded wings, echoing Ittan's tally book. Neela counts them twice and tells no one yet.
facts.why: plants clue C22 toward the crown leaf hinge.

facts.fact: The reading of all 41 caged odiyans' pages is done cage by cage that afternoon; each page is left in the straw. Cages stay shut.
facts.why: needed so Neela ends holding only the green quire and contract books.
